Microstructure, phase composition, mechanical properties and oxidation behavior of NbTaTi and NbTaZr ternary equiatomic alloys were studied.

The alloys were produced by arc melting and then hot isostatic pressed under the 210 MPa pressure of high purity argon at 1400 °C for 3 h prior to the testing. The density of NbTaTi was 10.1 g/cm3 and NbTaZr was 10.3 g/cm3.

The NbTaTi and NbTaZr were prepared by vacuum arc melting from the high purity (≥99.9%) elements. Each alloy was solidified inside a copper cavity, where it was prepared, and had a flattened cigar shape.

After solidification, the alloy samples were wrapped in a Ta foil and hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) under a hydrostatic pressure of a high purity argon of 210 MPa at 1400 °C for 3 h. Heating and cooling rates were 15 °C/min.

The microstructure of NbTaTi consists of the BCC matrix with coarse, ~0.4 mm in diameter grains and intragranular, needle-like, Ti-rich precipitates, which have a BCC crystal structure and their volume fraction is ~13%.
intragranular, needle-like, Ti-rich precipitates, which have a BCC crystal structure and their volume fraction is ~13%
There is also a small fraction of grain-boundary, Ti- and N-rich precipitates with a FCC crystal structure.
A co-continuous mixture of two coherent BCC phases, one being rich in Ta and another rich in Zr, is present inside the transformed grains in the form of nano-meter sized lamellae.
A co-continuous mixture of two coherent BCC phases, one being rich in Ta and another rich in Zr, is present inside the transformed grains in the form of nano-meter sized lamellae.
The microstructure of NbTaTi consists of the BCC matrix with coarse, ~0.4 mm in diameter grains and intragranular, needle-like, Ti-rich precipitates
The microstructure of NbTaZr consists of transformed grains of the high-temperature BCC phase with the average grain size of ~0.04 mm.
This microstructure is thought to be produced by spinodal decomposition of the high-temperature BCC phase.
